steam_pipe.title: Pipe / vent steam jet
steam_pipe.size_note: vertical jet from a 0.2 m vent, plume 1.5 to 2 m tall, clear gap about 10 to 20 cm

main.encoding: WebP lossy RGBA; rgb = grey, sRGB-encoded (use an sRGB texture); alpha = straight (non-premultiplied) coverage
main.blend: normal: (SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); or premultiply on load and use (ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)

scatter.encoding: grey WebP, same frame order as main at 0.5x size (low: 0.25x); value = forward-scatter strength 0..1
scatter.blend: additive on top of main: out += sunColour * scatter * sunBacklight * gain; mask with the main alpha so it never extends past the sprite

heat.encoding: grey WebP at 0.25x; heat = (value/255)^(1/0.8); 1.0 = th_ref kelvin above ambient

steam_pipe.anchor_note: anchor = [u, v] of the emitter / ground contact inside a frame, from the top-left corner

wind.note: plume bends over: lean the quad about its anchor
wind.note_base: plume bends over: lean the quad about its anchor

night.note: steam is lit by fires and lamps only: add the local light colour

thermal.note: steam is bright in thermal view: draw the heat layer through a white-hot palette, scaled by the alpha; the visible fog is irrelevant to the sensor

night_vision.note: steam is a soft grey cloud; add the scatter layer at 0.5 where IR illuminators hit it

haze.note: attach a DIST.haze source above the vent: strength, radius_m and height_m (the invisible hot gas is hotter than the visible plume), drifting up at rise_speed_mps; fade with the stage (start ramps in, fade ramps out)

mirror_variants.note: every loop clip may also be drawn mirrored (scale.x = -1) for twice as many looks; variants above are distinct simulation windows

night.note: fog glows only where lamps and headlights hit it

thermal.note: fog is faint and cool in thermal view: alpha x 0.10 in the cold end of the palette; it slightly blurs what is behind it

night_vision.note: fog scatters the illuminator back: add scatter x 0.8 plus alpha x 0.35 as a uniform veil and lower the contrast of what is behind it by alpha x 0.5

state_machine.description: form: cooling air makes fog thicken (play 'form' once, 8 key frames, cross-fade between them, then switch to 'drift'). drift: the normal moving fog (loop 'drift_a'/'drift_b'). linger: a calm period, nearly static slow churn (loop 'linger'). thin: burn-off, sun warms the air and the fog thins and breaks up (play 'thin' once, fade out at the end, delete the sprite). fall: the fog sinks and flattens (play 'fall' once, then hold its last frame as a thin low layer, then 'linger').
state_machine.crossfade: clips are different sims: cross-fade 0.5 to 1.5 s when switching; key-frame clips (form, thin, fall) play at 1 to 2 fps with interpolate: true (blend adjacent frames)

fog.scroll_note: the mean drift u_ref is baked OUT of the frames (the fog is Galilean-stabilised so loops are seamless): scroll the strip at u_ref plus the game wind to restore the motion
fog.vertical_note: frame bottom = ground level; sink the quad about 5 to 10 percent of its height into the ground

mirror_variants.note: every loop clip may also be drawn mirrored (scale.x = -1) for twice as many looks; variants above are distinct simulation windows

night_vision.note: fog scatters the illuminator back: add scatter x 0.8 plus alpha x 0.35 as a uniform veil and lower the contrast of what is behind it by alpha x 0.5

state_machine.description: form: cooling air makes fog thicken (play 'form' once, 8 key frames, cross-fade between them, then switch to 'drift'). drift: the normal moving fog (loop 'drift_a'/'drift_b'). linger: a calm period, nearly static slow churn (loop 'linger'). thin: burn-off, sun warms the air and the fog thins and breaks up (play 'thin' once, fade out at the end, delete the sprite). fall: the fog sinks and flattens (play 'fall' once, then hold its last frame as a thin low layer, then 'linger').
state_machine.crossfade: clips are different sims: cross-fade 0.5 to 1.5 s when switching; key-frame clips (form, thin, fall) play at 1 to 2 fps with interpolate: true (blend adjacent frames)

fog.scroll_note: the mean drift u_ref is baked OUT of the frames (the fog is Galilean-stabilised so loops are seamless): scroll the strip at u_ref plus the game wind to restore the motion
fog.vertical_note: frame bottom = ground level; sink the quad about 5 to 10 percent of its height into the ground

mirror_variants.note: every loop clip may also be drawn mirrored (scale.x = -1) for twice as many looks; variants above are distinct simulation windows

fog_valley.title: Valley fog pooling
fog_valley.size_note: fog that has sunk to fill low ground under an inversion: flat top at 9 m, soft wisps above; strip 96 m x 24 m (512x128), tileable

main.encoding: WebP lossy RGBA; rgb = grey, sRGB-encoded (use an sRGB texture); alpha = straight (non-premultiplied) coverage
main.blend: normal: (SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); or premultiply on load and use (ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)

scatter.encoding: grey WebP, same frame order as main at 0.5x size (low: 0.25x); value = forward-scatter strength 0..1
scatter.blend: additive on top of main: out += sunColour * scatter * sunBacklight * gain; mask with the main alpha so it never extends past the sprite

fog_valley.anchor_note: anchor = [u, v] of the emitter / ground contact inside a frame, from the top-left corner

tile.note: left and right edges are neighbours in the simulation (periodic), so strips tile seamlessly; the bottom edge sits on the ground and fades to 0

wind.note: pooled fog barely moves: scroll slowly, wisps above faster
wind.note_base: pooled fog barely moves: scroll slowly, wisps above faster
